ritual: Comment 'UNDER MY FEET' if you'd take the tour

slides.text: THERE'S A BURIED CITY UNDER SEATTLE
June 6, 1889. A glue pot tipped over in a carpentry shop. The Great Seattle Fire burned the heart of the city.
Old Seattle sat on soggy tideflats. At high tide, toilets could erupt.
So when they rebuilt, they raised the streets one to two stories higher.
The old storefronts and sidewalks were sealed in underneath.
Glass tiles in the new sidewalks let a little daylight down into the dark.
In 1907 the city condemned the underground, afraid of bubonic plague.
For decades it was left to rot.
In 1965 a local writer, Bill Speidel, started tours. You can still walk it today.
